name: fill-sum
axis: hot-loop element write + read on a pre-allocated i32 array; per-access bounds-check cost
nPython: N=2000000 elements, ROUNDS=20 (10x fewer rounds; multiply Python's wall time by 10 to compare)
notes: The array is allocated ONCE (N pushes) and then rewritten in place every round, so growth/allocation is outside the steady-state loop. Accumulator is i64 in VL/Rust, a plain Number in JS and a plain int in Python; the total (1.3e13) is exact in all four (< 2^53). Extra file `toplevel.vl` is the SAME algorithm written as a top-level script (every binding a module global instead of a function local) to quantify the globals cliff. Scale-verified by doubling ROUNDS: vl 1.97x, js 2.05x, py 2.13x, rs ~1.97x (Rust's absolute time is ~0.1s so its ratio is noise-sensitive; a 25/50/100/200/400 sweep is linear with a ~6ms intercept).

audit.startupFloor: Rust column is 90ms (min-of-5/7, taskset -c 2) = 8% process launcher; under the 200ms floor. Subtract the 6.8ms empty-Rust baseline before quoting a Rust:VL multiple. measured empty-program startup on this box (min-of-5, taskset -c 2): rustc-O binary 6.8ms, deno 19.3ms, python3 12.5ms, `vl run <prebuilt.wasm>` 10.6ms.
audit.rustVectorised: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT — rustc -O AUTO-VECTORISES this loop and no meta note said so. Confirmed by disassembling `main::main`: the hot loop is SSE2 packed integer arithmetic (54 packed ops in main::main). rustc's default target is baseline x86-64, so this is 128-bit SSE2; `rustc -O -C target-cpu=native` widens it further. The Rust:VL multiple on this benchmark is therefore mostly SIMD WIDTH, not scalar codegen quality — VL emits no SIMD. Report it as such.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
